q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer: the data does not actually show ROAS rising versus yesterday — Net ROAS fell from 1.21x on 2026-10-13 to 0.99x on 2026-10-14 — but it is above its recent "usual" level (0.99x vs a usual 0.83x, +19.1%). Net profit did fall sharply: ₹10,678 → ₹-289 (−103.0%). In plain terms: ROAS is only higher than the longer-term baseline, while profit dropped vs the prior day because contribution margin fell more than ad spend.

What changed (largest impacts first)
- Contribution margin collapsed: contribution margin fell from ₹61,121 to ₹47,101 (−22.9%); this reduced net profit far more than the small ad-spend change helped. Why it matters: lower margin directly cuts profit even if some marketing became relatively more efficient.
- Ad spend (P&L basis) eased slightly: ₹50,443 → ₹47,390 (−6.1%). This lowered spend but not enough to offset the margin drop; it moved profit less than the contribution-margin fall.
- Web traffic/events are flagged as a supported driver of the profit decline: web events moved from 53,625 → 35,338 (−34.1%) and the diagnosis estimates this plausibly explains a large part of the net profit drop. In short, fewer valuable events (visits/engagements) lowered sales and margins.
- Campaign-level divergence: some campaigns (e.g. Brand Search) improved ROAS and profit, while others lost orders and margin — the net effect was a big margin loss despite pockets of higher ROAS.

Worth checking: drill to campaign- and product-level contribution margin and orders for 2026-10-13 vs 2026-10-14 to see which campaigns lost orders/margin and whether returns/taxes or product costs changed.

Period: 2026-10-13..2026-10-14 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-15
